rationale: Both responses rest on the right principle: immutable generation artifacts kept separate from append-only grading records, so regrading never requires regeneration. Both also use content addressing, schema versions and derived, rebuildable indexes. A's content-addressed generation blob embeds run_id while its hash excludes it. That means two runs sharing a hash would need different bytes at the same path, undermining both dedup and immutability. Its reconstruct code also reads a field the evaluation record lacks. A contributes useful details: unique constraints for idempotent grading, a required grader-version filter, and a note on retention GC. B is more internally consistent and rigorous. Every hop in the reconstruction chain is a hash, covering prompt, output, model config, environment snapshot and suite definition. It stores the grader's actual input separately from the raw output, a sharp insight for regrading. It verifies hashes on read so the integrity guarantee is real, keeps a per-version schema registry, dedupes at the run-spec level before launch, includes volume math, and pins Docker image digests. B has only a minor example typo (a repeated prompt hash), so it is the sounder design.
